verdict.root_cause: Checkout requests fail at the shipping-quote hop: checkoutservice's ShippingService/GetQuote client span carries ERROR in every sampled trace while the shippingservice server span and its own outbound HTTP client span complete cleanly [tr_051ad5125850]. Failures are fast (<4ms on the failing hop, 9-12ms end to end), so this is a rejected/unusable response at the checkout->shipping boundary, not a stall or timeout. Order preparation short-circuits there, so payment, email and order-placement never run - matching the log pattern where late-window orders show placement entries but no payment/email/message-write completions [tr_e11d26c58693], and explaining why accountingservice, emailservice, frauddetectionservice and quoteservice alerted three minutes later as downstream-of-checkout consumers. No checkoutservice change is recorded in the searched interval [tr_3137962dea86][tr_351a425bc187], and the change window queried started at onset rather than before it, so the originating change for the shipping/quote path was never examined. Best reading of the mechanism: the shipping-quote contract or endpoint configuration on the checkout->shippingservice/quoteservice path yields a response checkoutservice rejects - a wrong value in the call path, not exhaustion or slowness.
verdict.reasoning: Traces localize the error boundary precisely to the checkoutservice-side GetQuote client span with a healthy server span beneath it [tr_051ad5125850], which rules out an internal shippingservice fault and points at the request/response contract or endpoint settings used by checkout for that hop. Logs corroborate the truncation point: placements continue but all post-quote steps vanish [tr_e11d26c58693]. Latency and exhaustion are excluded by the sub-4ms failing hop and complete, untruncated traces [tr_051ad5125850], and checkoutservice's error ratio shows no step change at onset [tr_e3bb2d6e66a5]. cartservice is exonerated on the request path (sub-ms, error-free cart spans) despite image churn that reverted off the hotfix an hour before onset [tr_572b0a3b588d][tr_c19be514f390]. Confidence is low because no dispatch ever examined shippingservice or quoteservice directly and both change queries covered only post-onset time [tr_351a425bc187].
open_questions: What error code/message does checkoutservice's GetQuote client span carry? No log or span attribute was retrieved naming the failure.
Were there changes to shippingservice or quoteservice in the hours before 04:32:45? Both change queries covered only the post-onset window.
Why did quoteservice alert at 04:36:15 - as a victim of checkout's failure or as the origin of the bad quote response? Never dispatched.
Did anything change in checkoutservice before 04:32:45? The pre-onset change surface is entirely unobserved.

alternatives.root_cause: quoteservice or shippingservice returns a malformed or out-of-contract quote payload that checkoutservice rejects, making the fault originate downstream.
alternatives.why_not: No dispatch touched quoteservice or shippingservice; the only observed spans for shippingservice are error-free, and quoteservice alerted after checkout rather than before, so it reads as downstream. Plausible but wholly unevidenced.

alternatives.root_cause: A bad artifact reached the shipping-quote path via the platform-automation image flip-flop, leaving a version whose quote response checkout cannot parse.
alternatives.why_not: The only recorded image churn is on cartservice, and it reverted off the hotfix ~1h before onset [tr_572b0a3b588d]; no image change is recorded on any service in the failing path.

proposal.expected_effect: No action proposed, so no effect should be observed. The state to keep watching is unchanged: checkoutservice's ShippingService/GetQuote client span carrying ERROR in every sampled trace [tr_051ad5125850], and late-window checkout logs showing order-placement entries with no payment/email/message-write completions. Any remediation proposed later should be judged by those two signals returning to the early-window pattern (GetQuote client spans completing with OK, full placement->payment->email->message-write sequences resuming within one or two minutes).
proposal.if_wrong: This abstention is wrong if someone retrieves the missing evidence and it meets an action's preconditions: specifically (a) a change_history query on shippingservice or quoteservice covering the hours *before* 2026-09-20T04:32:45 that names a config/env/endpoint edit with a recorded prior value, or (b) the error code/message on the checkoutservice GetQuote client span naming a concrete contract or address mismatch. Either would convert this into a targeted revert_config on the service that actually changed. Until then, no permitted action's preconditions are met: revert_config requires a prior configuration in change history and a config change named inside the window, and the only change queries run were on checkoutservice (empty, and windowed from onset forward, so silent on pre-onset changes) [tr_3137962dea86][tr_351a425bc187] and cartservice (image flips only, already excluded as the failing hop by traces) [tr_051ad5125850].
proposal.risk: The risk of abstaining is that the outage continues: checkout is short-circuiting before payment on every sampled trace, so orders are being lost for as long as this stands. That is a real cost, not zero. The risk of the alternative — acting anyway — is worse and is why I abstain: the verdict is low confidence and names the wrong target. The evidence puts the error boundary on the *caller* side (checkoutservice's client span is ERROR while shippingservice's server span and its outbound HTTP client span both complete cleanly) [tr_051ad5125850], yet checkoutservice has no recorded prior configuration to revert to [tr_3137962dea86][tr_351a425bc187], and shippingservice/quoteservice were never queried at all. A revert_config aimed at shippingservice or quoteservice would be reverting a change nobody has evidence exists, and if the reverted value is a dependency address it would move traffic on a path that is currently serving its server-side spans without error — turning a one-hop failure into a broader one.
proposal.blast_radius: None from this proposal, since nothing is changed. For context on what a later action would touch: checkoutservice is called by frontend and fans out to cartservice, currencyservice, productcatalogservice, paymentservice; recreating it resets connections for frontend and therefore user-visible checkout. shippingservice is reached via quoteservice; changing either moves the quote path that accountingservice, emailservice and frauddetectionservice sit downstream of as checkout consumers.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Critical multi-service failure starting at checkoutservice with four downstream consumers alerting minutes later; nothing here can be dismissed and no open incident covers it. Fault class is not implied by the alert pattern alone, though checkout is the plausible origin.
